ig_caption:
Bidirectional Dijkstra: How Modern Route Planners Scale ⚡
Ever wonder how GPS avoids brute-force shortest paths?

Here’s the core idea of Bidirectional Dijkstra: instead of searching from the start only, we run two Dijkstra searches—one forward from the start, one backward from the destination. Each side expands using its own priority queue, and once their visited regions meet, we can reconstruct the shortest path with far fewer explored nodes.

🔥 What you’re seeing on the map: two colored frontiers converging.
- Forward search: grows cheapest distances outward from START
- Backward search: grows cheapest distances outward from GOAL
- Stop condition: when the best possible path through the meeting region can’t be improved

✅ Takeaway: same correctness as Dijkstra, but typically much faster in practice on large graphs—especially when you can stop early.

Debate it: In your experience, is bidirectional search always a win, or can overhead/graph structure flip the performance?
